title: Pseudo-coherence is preserved by direct summands
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K, L, and M be objects of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. If K is isomorphic to L \oplus M and K is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], then L and M are pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 08CE (pseudo-coherent complexes are closed under direct summands)

proof.text: Pseudo-coherence is local and passes to open subsets by [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], so it suffices to work on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ of $X$, where $K|_U\cong L|_U\oplus M|_U$ and $K|_U$ is pseudo-coherent. First, all three objects lie in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U)$: locally $K|_U$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free modules, whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent, so each $H^i(K|_U)$ is quasi-coherent; $H^i(L|_U)$ and $H^i(M|_U)$ are direct summands of $H^i(K|_U)$, i.e. images of idempotent endomorphisms of a quasi-coherent module, hence quasi-coherent (elementary). By the equivalence $D(R)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U)$ of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] choose complexes $P^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ of $R$-modules with $L|_U\cong\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ and $M|_U\cong\widetilde{Q^\bullet}$; as the functor is additive, $K|_U\cong\widetilde{P^\bullet\oplus Q^\bullet}$. By [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] applied to $P^\bullet\oplus Q^\bullet$, the complex $P^\bullet\oplus Q^\bullet$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules. The last clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-summand] gives the same for $P^\bullet$ and $Q^\bullet$, and [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] again shows that $L|_U$ and $M|_U$ are pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 08CE, reduction from the scheme statement to affine module complexes

proof.text: The bounded-above finite-free representatives obtained on each affine U witness that L and M are pseudo-coherent on X by the local definition [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. The argument applies independently to both summands, and the zero-summand cases are immediate.
